title: HubSpot Calling vs Aircall for Sales Teams — Jon Martin
seoTitle: HubSpot Calling vs Aircall: Minutes, Plans, and CTI
description: HubSpot's built-in calling versus Aircall for HubSpot sales teams: included minutes, seats, prices, and what logs to the record. Checked Nov 23, 2026.
h1: HubSpot calling vs Aircall for sales teams
dek: HubSpot already includes calling. The question is whether the minutes you pay for cover your team, or whether you need a phone system that sits on top of the CRM.
This page lines up HubSpot's built-in dialer against Aircall so you can decide on capacity first and features second.

blocks.html: HubSpot includes calling in Sales Hub and Service Hub. Minutes are a shared account cap, not a per-rep allotment: 500 calling minutes per account per month on Starter, 3,000 calling minutes per account per month on Professional, and 12,000 calling minutes per account per month on Enterprise.

Aircall is a separate cloud phone system with a native HubSpot integration. On its published US plans, Essentials is $30 per license per month, billed annually and Professional is $50 per license per month, billed annually, with 3 licenses minimum on every plan and unlimited calls within the US and Canada on Essentials and Professional (terms apply).
Stay on HubSpot calling if your monthly talk time fits the included minutes. Add Aircall if you are hitting the cap or need a full phone system. Decide on capacity before you decide on features.

sections.label: What good looks like for a HubSpot dialer

items: You know the monthly minute cap before you start a calling block.
Calls land on the right HubSpot records with recording and outcome.
Outcomes can trigger HubSpot workflows so follow-up is not manual.

blocks.html: If a call never lands on the record, the pipeline report is fiction. That is the filter for this comparison.
On HubSpot, calling is included in Sales Hub and Service Hub Starter, Professional, and Enterprise. The useful detail is that minutes are pooled, not handed out per user.

items: Minutes: 500 calling minutes per account per month on Starter, 3,000 calling minutes per account per month on Professional, and 12,000 calling minutes per account per month on Enterprise.
Pooling: minutes are not additive across hubs: Sales Hub Professional plus Service Hub Professional is still 3,000 minutes per account per month.
Reset: minutes reset at the start of each month, not on your renewal date, and once they run out you can't start new calls from HubSpot.
Seats: an assigned Sales or Service seat is needed to call on Professional and Enterprise; on Starter, a Core Seat can also call.
Watch the meter: calling through your own phone uses twice as many minutes, because it makes two separate calls.
Numbers: 1 HubSpot-provided phone number on Starter, up to 3 on Professional, and up to 5 on Enterprise.

blocks.html: If you run out, you can add capacity on the higher editions. The catalog lists $50 a month for each extra 1,000 calling minutes, on Sales Hub or Service Hub Professional or Enterprise only, and $25 a month for 5 more HubSpot-provided phone numbers, on Professional or Enterprise only. Light inbound or booked calls usually stay inside the cap. Heavy outbound does not.
On the dialer itself, the sales power dialer is labeled beta and is listed for Sales Hub Enterprise. If you need queued outbound today, read the Aircall section before you plan around that beta.

sections.label: Aircall as the HubSpot phone system

blocks.html: Aircall is a cloud phone system for sales and support. On HubSpot, the part that matters is the logging.

items: On HubSpot, calls are logged on Contact, Company, Deal, and Ticket records with duration, number, a recording link, comments, outcomes, and transcription.
Insight Cards show HubSpot history before a rep answers.

blocks.html: Integrations: Aircall's pricing page says all plans include 250+ integrations, HubSpot among them.

items: Essentials: $30 per license per month, billed annually (annual billing is 25% off monthly). 3 licenses minimum on every plan. Essentials includes 250+ integrations, IVR, call recording, and SMS.
Professional: $50 per license per month, billed annually. Professional adds advanced analytics, smart routing, Power Dialer, and AI conversation intelligence.
Enterprise: custom pricing, for teams of 25+ licenses, with unlimited global calls on Enterprise.
Extra numbers: $6 per month for each extra number.
AI Voice Agents are sold standalone from $99 per month minimum, with 50 AI Voice Agents minutes a month on every plan.
Call data lands where HubSpot reporting and workflows already look.
Unlimited US and Canada calling on the published plans, so you are not rationing a shared pool.
A real Power Dialer and smart routing when you outgrow click-to-call.
Another subscription on top of HubSpot, with a three-license minimum.
Someone has to own routing, properties, and ticket rules.
Overkill if a few short calls a month already fit inside your included minutes.

blocks.html: Deeper write-up: Aircall for HubSpot teams.

items: Estimate a rough monthly talk time. If it fits the included minutes, stay on HubSpot calling.
If you are hitting the cap, add capacity on Professional or Enterprise, or move the calling to Aircall.
If you need IVR, a power dialer, or calling that is not minute-capped, pick Aircall (Essentials or Professional).
Before you buy either, decide which HubSpot objects get call activity and who owns the routing rules.

blocks.html: This is a capacity and feature decision, not a moral one. There is no prize for ripping out calling you already pay for. For a broader list of options, see my roundup of calling apps for HubSpot.
